best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows That Opened in 2020

As we look back in March 2026 at the Broadway season of 2020, a year that would soon be disrupted by unprecedented challenges, we find a collection of productions that showcased the theater's commitment to both bold reimagining and vital storytelling.

The standout among these offerings is **Les Misérables**, which earns the highest critical marks with its grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This darker interpretation of the beloved musical demonstrates that even the most familiar stories can find new resonance through fresh artistic vision, though the approach doesn't win over every critic.

**A Soldier's Play** represents perhaps the season's most significant theatrical event—Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally receiving its long-overdue Broadway premiere. The production's powerful examination of race and justice within the military proves as urgent and relevant as when Fuller first wrote it, with critics praising the stellar revival for its continued resonance.

Meanwhile, **West Side Story** arrives in Ivo van Hove's characteristically radical reimagining, proving deeply divisive. Some critics embrace the bold visual design and visceral energy, while others question whether the experimental approach serves or obscures the classic material.

Rounding out the season are Laura Linney's luminous solo performance in **My Name is Lucy Barton**—an adaptation that generates mixed responses despite her acclaimed work—and **Grand Horizons**, a well-acted if familiar comedy elevated by Broadway veterans Jane Alexander and James Cromwell.

With an average critical score of 74/100 across these five productions, the early 2020 season offers theatergoers a mix of innovative revivals and intimate new works that continue to reward audiences six years later.

# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted—productions that launched just before or during one of the most tumultuous periods in Broadway history. Despite the challenges, these five shows demonstrate the range and ambition that defined the season.

Leading our rankings is a reimagined **Les Misérables** (83/100), which earns critical acclaim for its grittier approach at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, though the bold reinvention doesn't win over all traditionalists. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** (78/100) finally brings Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway in a revival that critics widely celebrate as both overdue and essential, with its examination of race and power in the military proving as urgent as ever.

The remaining productions showcase Broadway's diversity of voices and styles. Laura Linney anchors **My Name is Lucy Barton** (71/100), an intimate solo adaptation that polarizes critics—some find it a luminous character study, while others question its theatrical impact. **Grand Horizons** (71/100) offers more traditional boulevard comedy about late-life divorce, with Jane Alexander's performance elevating familiar material. Meanwhile, **West Side Story** (68/100) proves the most divisive entry, as director Ivo van Hove's radical reimagining with video design and unconventional staging splits critical opinion sharply between those embracing innovation and those missing Robbins' choreography.

With an average score of 74/100 across these five productions, the 2020 season—truncated as it was—delivered thoughtful, ambitious work. Explore the full reviews to discover which of these distinctive productions aligns with your theatrical tastes.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2021 represent a remarkable period of theatrical innovation and resilience. That year marked Broadway's emotional return following the pandemic shutdown, and the season delivered an impressive collection of work that critics scored at an average of 81/100.

The standout among these productions is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama that earns the highest critical score (86/100) for its mesmerizing approach to true-crime storytelling, featuring Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance. Close behind, **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** (83/100) transforms the Playhouse Theatre itself into an immersive nightclub experience, with Rebecca Frecknall's acclaimed reimagining breathing new life into the classic musical. Meanwhile, **The Lehman Trilogy** (81/100) receives widespread praise as an epic theatrical triumph, tracing 163 years of American capitalism through extraordinary performances and stunning stagecraft.

The season showcases remarkable diversity in form and content—from verbatim FBI transcripts in **Is This a Room** to Ruben Santiago-Hudson's virtuosic solo turn in **Lackawanna Blues**, from the exuberant pop feminism of **SIX** to the urgent contemporary drama of **Pass Over**, which notably served as Broadway's first show back after the shutdown. Gender-swapped revivals like Marianne Elliott's **Company** demonstrate how fresh perspectives can revitalize canonical works, while **The Phantom of the Opera** proves that spectacle and melody never go out of style.

Whether you're drawn to experimental docudrama, immersive reimaginings, or intimate character studies, these ten productions offer a comprehensive view of what made 2021 a defining year for Broadway.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable period of theatrical achievement, delivering an exceptional collection of new productions and revivals that continue to resonate with audiences years later.

The season's crown jewel is undoubtedly **Kimberly Akimbo**, David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori's quirky musical about a teenager with a rare aging condition. Critics consistently hail it as a near-perfect work that masterfully balances laugh-out-loud comedy with profound emotional depth. Close behind, **Into the Woods** offers a stripped-down revival that serves as a triumphant tribute to Stephen Sondheim, featuring stellar performances that honor the late composer's legacy. Meanwhile, **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical, earns widespread acclaim for its brazenly original and brutally honest exploration of Black queer identity.

What makes this collection particularly noteworthy is the prevalence of Pulitzer Prize-winning works. The season brought major revivals of **Topdog/Underdog** by Suzan-Lori Parks, **Between Riverside and Crazy** by Stephen Adler Guirgis, **How I Learned to Drive** by Paula Vogel, and **Cost of Living** by Martyna Majok—all Pulitzer winners that found new life on Broadway stages. Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt** and Jordan E. Cooper's audacious satire **Ain't No Mo'** further demonstrate the season's range, from Holocaust meditation to provocative comedy.

With an impressive average critic score of 83/100 across these ten productions, the 2022 season represents a high-water mark for Broadway's commitment to both artistic excellence and diverse storytelling. Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting favorites, this collection offers essential viewing for any serious theater enthusiast.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the theatrical legacy of 2023 continues to resonate on Broadway, with several productions still captivating audiences more than two years after their debuts. This collection of ten plays represents an exceptional period for non-musical theatre, averaging an impressive 82/100 critical score and showcasing remarkable range—from intimate solo performances to sweeping ensemble dramas.

The year's theatrical highlights demonstrate Broadway's capacity for both artistic redemption and bold new voices. Maria Friedman's revival of **Merrily We Roll Along** leads the pack, finally vindicating Sondheim's famously troubled 1981 musical with an emotionally resonant production that critics consider definitive. Close behind, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** proves that intellectual property adaptations can transcend their source material, delivering technically stunning theatre that West End audiences first embraced before its Broadway transfer.

The season's strength extends well beyond these headliners. Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's **Appropriate** emerges as a modern American classic, featuring Sarah Paulson in a searing family drama that dissects inherited racism and familial dysfunction. Meanwhile, the long-overdue revival of **Purlie Victorious** demonstrates how Ossie Davis's 1961 satire remains bracingly relevant, and **Parade** finds urgent contemporary resonance in its historical tragedy. The diversity of voices and stories—from Alex Edelman's solo show **Just for Us** to James Ijames's Pulitzer-winning **Fat Ham**—underscores 2023 as a watershed year for American playwriting.

Whether you're drawn to reimagined classics, technically ambitious spectacles, or intimate storytelling, these productions offer compelling reasons to experience the enduring power of Broadway's dramatic tradition.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the shows that premiered in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This curated collection of ten productions—ranging from intimate character studies to sweeping musicals—maintains an impressive average critic score of 83/100, reflecting a particularly strong theatrical season.

Leading the rankings is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's acclaimed drama about a 1970s rock band in the studio, which critics consistently describe as a theatrical marvel for its authentic portrayal of the creative process. The show's meticulous attention to period detail and nuanced exploration of artistic collaboration have made it a critical darling. Close behind, **Operation Mincemeat** proves that grassroots productions can compete with Broadway's biggest names, earning praise for its inventive energy and ensemble work following its West End transfer.

The diversity of this season's offerings is notable. **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's irreverent reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist, provides sharp comedic relief, while **Mary Jane** offers an intimate, understated portrait of maternal devotion in the face of medical crisis. Meanwhile, **Maybe Happy Ending** brings unexpected emotional depth to a robot love story, and classic revivals like **Gypsy** and **Oliver!** demonstrate how fresh directorial perspectives can breathe new life into beloved material.

Whether you're drawn to innovative new works like Justin Peck's dance-driven **Illinoise** or educational entertainment such as **Suffs**' suffrage movement chronicle, this season offers something for every theatrical taste. Browse the full rankings to find your next Broadway experience.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As March 2026 arrives, Broadway's 2025 play season continues to resonate with audiences, showcasing a remarkable range of theatrical excellence. From bold revivals of American classics to innovative new works, the season demonstrates the enduring power of straight plays to captivate and challenge theatergoers.

Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons** leads the field, earning widespread critical acclaim for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work. Arthur Miller's post-war family drama proves as relevant as ever in van Hove's stripped-down staging, which critics praise for its raw, powerful approach to the material.

The season also celebrates theatrical nostalgia with **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee**, whose 20th-anniversary revival critics hail as joyous and perfectly timed. The beloved musical-comedy hybrid reminds audiences why it became an off-Broadway phenomenon, with its airtight writing and emotional depth earning fresh appreciation.

Family audiences find enchantment in **Paddington The Musical**, where a remarkably lifelike bear puppet becomes what critics call a theatrical marvel. Meanwhile, new American voices shine through works like Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English** and Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' **Purpose**, both delivering sharp, incisive examinations of identity and family dynamics.

The season's average critic score of 84/100 across these ten productions reflects a strong year for dramatic theater, with works ranging from David Wohl's ambitious feminist memory play **Liberation** to the darkly comic musical **Dead Outlaw**. A timely revival of **Ragtime** rounds out the offerings, with Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance earning particular praise.

Whether you're drawn to classic American drama, innovative new voices, or family-friendly spectacle, this season's plays offer compelling reasons to experience live theater.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings a notably lean opening schedule for new Broadway plays, with just one production making its debut this month. While the limited roster reflects the challenging economics facing straight plays on Broadway, the sole entry demonstrates the enduring appeal of well-crafted psychological drama.

**Bug** stands as the month's singular offering, marking the long-awaited Broadway premiere of Tracy Letts' 1996 psychological thriller. With a solid critic score of 74/100 across 35 reviews, the production earns mostly positive notices for its intense exploration of paranoia and delusion. Originally produced by Chicago's Red Orchid Theatre three decades ago, the play arrives on Broadway with renewed relevance, its themes of conspiracy and fractured reality resonating in contemporary discourse. Critics particularly praise the production's claustrophobic staging and committed performances, though some note the material's deliberately unsettling nature may not appeal to all theatergoers.

The sparse March schedule underscores a broader trend in commercial theater, where plays increasingly struggle to secure Broadway berths amid rising production costs and risk-averse producers. That **Bug** makes it to the Great White Way at all speaks to both the strength of Letts' reputation—bolstered by his Pulitzer Prize-winning **August: Osage County**—and the theater community's ongoing commitment to provocative, challenging work.

For audiences seeking substantive dramatic fare this month, **Bug** offers a compelling if confronting option that showcases the raw power of theatrical storytelling. Those planning their spring theater calendar should consider catching this production while monitoring announcements for upcoming play openings in the months ahead.
